Exact recovery under a degree-restricted adversary Another interesting consequence of the above analysis is that in case we allow no corrupted vertices (i.e. M = ∅), but continue to allow an adversary to arbitrarily corrupt up to ε(deg) k edges incident to every vertex in [n], then our algorithm still achieves exact recovery and our pseudo-concentration implies that ST is always a subset of some Sℓ .14 This is interesting not only because it yields a more robust algorithm for exact recovery as described previously, but also because the used techniques might prove useful for finding algorithms in other noisy settings, including a more noisy version of RIGs where not only additional edges outside of the ground-truth cliques can form, but also some edges within the Sℓ might be missing due to noise. We leave studying this case open for future work, but believe that our techniques form a good starting point. We refer to Appendix G for more details.

Comparison to the algorithms for the FK-model Finally, we discuss how our model relates to the semi-random setting considered by Buhai et al. (2023), where algorithms robust agains a monotone adversary for the so-called Feige-Kilian model (FK-model) are introduced. Here, a clique S of size k is planted in an initially empty graph, while the edges in S × [n] \ S are present independently with probability pFK , and edges in [n] \ S × [n] \ S are entirely arbitrary. The goal is to find a list of (1 + o(1))n/k cliques that includes S. One may wonder if our model can be seen as a special case of the FK-model if the edges in [n]\S ×[n]\S are chosen appropriately and pFK is sufficiently large. While the models are certainly related, the biggest difference to our setting is that in the FK model for pFK being bounded away from 1, any clique can intersect the ground-truth S in at most O(log(n)) vertices. In RIG(n, d, p, q), 1 the typical overlap between any two Sℓ , Sℓ′ is ≈ kδ, which is of order nΩ(1) if k ⩾ n 2 +ε . To potentially be able to map between FK and RIG(n, d, p, q), we would therefore need to choose pFK quite close to one in order to achieve δk × k-sized bicliques in G[S ⊎ ([n] \ S)]. Specifically, this would require (1 − pFK )−1 ≳ δk/ log(n), as a simple calculation reveals. 1 1
